skill_name: Distributed Systems, Message Brokers & Event Driven Architecture
subtopic: Transactional Outbox Pattern and Change Data Capture (CDC)
question_text: [Distributed Systems, Message Brokers & Event Driven Architecture - Q43] How does the Transactional Outbox Pattern solve the dual-write problem between a relational database and a message broker (e.g. Kafka)?

options.text: By executing a distributed 2-Phase Commit (2PC) between database and Kafka
By inserting outgoing events into an `outbox` table within the same local database transaction as business entities, and using an asynchronous CDC relay to publish to Kafka
By publishing to Kafka first and rolling back Kafka if the database fails
By disabling transactions in the database

answer_explanation: Because both entity state and outbox event are saved in the same local ACID transaction, either both commit or neither commits, eliminating dual-write inconsistency.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Because both entity state and outbox event are saved in the same local ACID transaction, either both commit or neither commits, eliminating dual-write inconsistency.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
